text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Spike detected: unusual high QPS on /v1/embeddings (ingress gateway). 3.2M reqs in last 10m, sources concentrated from several ASN blocks. Possible scraper / credential stuffing pattern. Auto-throttles triggered but error % rising. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/XYz123 (alert 4267).

sanjeev: acked. i'm on call. digging into which keys/paths are hot. can someone paste the top IPs and key ids?

maria: top ips (sample):
```
- 34.102.11.0/24
- 104.238.220.0/24
- 185.199.108.0/24
```
keys: mostly public-ish keys (no customer org id) and some older API keys with high usage from same UA string "curl/7.85.0". Looks like automated scrapers hitting embeddings endpoints.

aj: adding packet-level view, confirmed same src ASN (AS15169 & AS39848), requests pattern = very short TTL, high token per request = small but repeated embedding calls.

sanjeev: impact? customers?

maria: latency up to 700ms p95 on embeddings route, token cost skyrocketing. Several customers in tryout tier reported 429s. No authenticated enterprise incidents reported yet. Support tickets: 5 customers complaining about intermittent 429s, one with high volume (acct: tryout-451).

ops-oncall: paging infra to prepare mitigations. i'm going to attempt progressive mitigations: 1) tighten inline WAF rule to drop matching UA + IP ranges; 2) apply burst rate limit on embeddings route for anonymous/tryout keys; 3) enable extra caching for repeated small inputs. will coordinate with security.

security-bot: Suggested WAF rule id 9987 (block UA pattern "curl/7\..*" when from listed IP ranges). Q: any false-positive risk?

maria: low FP risk for that UA/IP combo right now. but we should not block enterprise keys. we need key-level allowlist check.

sanjeev: ok implement in this order. disa, can infra push WAF and rate-limit? share commands so we can audit.

disa: on it. Pushing WAF rule now. CLI: 
```
# add WAF rule (apply only to embeddings-route)
redwood-wafctl add-rule --name "block-scraper-176220" --match "ua =~ /curl\/7\\..*/ && src_cidr in (34.102.11.0/24,104.238.220.0/24,185.199.108.0/24)" --action block
```
Applying... (will scope to route /v1/embeddings, not global).

disa: rule applied: waf-rule-id=wr-176220-1 :white_check_mark: (Ratelimit and quota patch next).

ops-oncall: now applying rate-limit policy for tryout keys and anonymous tokens. Config snippet: 
```
# ephemeral config
route: /v1/embeddings
policy:
  tier: tryout
  window: 60s
  requests: 50  # temporary hard cap
  burst: 10
```
Pushing via gateway API: `curl -X POST https://gateway.internal/acl/policies -d @policy.json -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN"`

ops-oncall: policy pushed. Monitoring effect.

maria: immediate drop in unusual QPS by ~65% in first 90s. p95 latency down to 220ms. Errors (5xx) trending down.

support-ledger: reported 3 of the 5 complaining customers saw 429s after the rate-limit change (expected). I reached out to explain temporary mitigation and offered token white-listing for impacted paid users. They accepted an allowlist for tryout-451.

sanjeev: good catch. for the allowlist we need to add tryout-451 and one other paid org. disa can you add those to a temporary bypass? Also, record the allowlist ids for rollback.

disa: added bypass for keys: tryout-451, enterprise-1902. Command used: `redwood-acl add-exception --policy-id p-176220 --key tryout-451` -> success.

security-bot: Also suggests adding a geo-shaping rule to favor region-based rate limits for the embeddings route (because sources mostly from EU edge points). Recommend temporary geo-throttle: non-customer traffic from EU/AS block lowered to 20 req/min.

aj: ran a quick correlation with login attempts — no spike in auth failures, so not classic credential stuffing. It's more of a scraper / cheap-key abuse.

sanjeev: action summary (for runbook):
- WAF rule wr-176220-1 applied (blocked UA/IP combo).
- Rate-limit policy p-176220 applied to tryout/anonymous keys.
- Temporary exceptions added for tryout-451, enterprise-1902.
- Monitoring dashboards pointed to recovery.

maria: results after 12m: overall QPS back to baseline, 429s localised. No additional 5xx. Cost spike reduced.

ops-oncall: i will keep the rate-limit in place for 2 hours then relax to test. schedule a canary relax: decrease restriction in steps.

support-ledger: will follow up with the 5 customers with a note and ETA for rollback. Draft msg: "We're mitigating an automated scraping activity that caused intermittent rate limiting on embeddings. We've implemented temporary protections; paid customers can request immediate whitelisting."

sanjeev: agreed. create incident ticket and assign postmortem. We need to answer: how did these keys abuse the system despite quotas? Consider tighter default quotas and UA/IP heuristics in onboarding.

maria: i'll capture request examples for the postmortem. sample payload pattern: repeated identical texts of 1-2 tokens, high frequency.

disa: note on change window: both WAF and rate-limit configs were pushed during 17:34-17:40 UTC. All changes logged under change-set cs-176220.

ops-oncall: alerting update: lowered alert sensitivity temporarily to avoid flapping during adjustment. will re-enable normal thresholds after 2h.

sanjeev: handoff — i will be primary owner for the postmortem. ops-oncall, monitor for 45m and ping if anything regresses.

ops-oncall: 45m monitoring started. so far stable. :thumbsup:

security-bot: queued a follow-up rule to throttle suspicious UA patterns for 30d or until postmortem closes.

support-ledger: closing loop with customers. one asked for more details on IPs blocked; we shared sanitized list and timelines.

sanjeev: final notes for thread: retrospective actions:
- enforce lower default tryout quotas and shorter burst window (assigned to product).
- add automated UA + src_cidr detection rule to WAF onboarding (security).
- add an integration test that simulates scraper patterns hitting embeddings to catch config gaps (eng-runtime).
- scheduled postmortem meeting tomorrow 1400 UTC.

maria: thanks all. closing incident thread unless something else comes up. :white_check_mark:
